A person qualifies to be appointed as a member of the Board under section 31 (1) (f) if the person— (a) is a citizen of Kenya; (b) holds a degree from a university recognized in Kenya; (c) has at least six years’ experience in resource mobilization, human resource development, business, financial management, governance, or other relevant professional experience; and (d) meets the requirements of Chapter Six of the Constitution.

explanation.en: This section sets out who can be appointed as a member of the Board under section 31 (1) (f). The person must be a Kenyan citizen, hold a degree from a university recognized in Kenya, and have at least six years' experience in resource mobilization, human resource development, business, financial management, governance, or other relevant professional work. The person must also meet the requirements of Chapter Six of the Constitution.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaweka masharti ya mtu kuteuliwa kuwa mjumbe wa Bodi chini ya kifungu cha 31 (1) (f). Mtu huyo awe raia wa Kenya, awe na shahada kutoka chuo kikuu kinachotambuliwa nchini Kenya, na awe na uzoefu wa angalau miaka sita katika uchangishaji rasilimali, maendeleo ya rasilimali watu, biashara, usimamizi wa fedha, utawala, ama uzoefu mwingine wa kitaaluma unaofaa. Pia atimize mahitaji ya Sura ya Sita ya Katiba.
explanation.sheng: Section 33 ina-set qualifications za person ku-be appointed kama member wa Board under section 31 (1) (f). Person lazima awe citizen wa Kenya, awe na degree kutoka university recognized in Kenya, na awe na at least six years experience kwa resource mobilization, human resource development, business, financial management, governance ama other relevant professional work. Pia lazima afikie requirements za Chapter Six ya Constitution.

neutral_check.note: Section only lists appointment qualifications for Board members; described as written, with no opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Vacancy of office.
clauses.text: 34. (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the office of the Chairperson and a member of the Board shall become vacant if the Chairperson or member– (a) resigns by notice in writing addressed to the appointing authority; (b) is absent from three consecutive meetings of the Board without the permission of the Chairperson, or, in the case of the Chairperson, the permission of the Cabinet Secretary; (c) is unable to exercise the function of the office by reason of physical or mental infirmity; (d) is adjudged bankrupt by a court of competent jurisdiction or enters into a composition or scheme of arrangement for the benefit of creditors; (e) is in breach of the requirements of Chapter Six of the Constitution; or (f) is convicted of an offence and sentenced to imprisonment for a period of six or more months.

explanation.en: Section 34 says when the office of the Chairperson or a member of the Board becomes vacant, meaning the person no longer holds the post. This happens if they resign by written notice to the appointing authority, or miss three Board meetings in a row without permission (from the Chairperson, or from the Cabinet Secretary in the Chairperson's case). It also happens if they cannot do the job because of physical or mental illness or disability, or are declared bankrupt by a court or make an arrangement with their creditors. Finally, the office falls vacant if they breach the requirements of Chapter Six of the Constitution (on leadership and integrity), or are convicted of an offence and sentenced to prison for six months or more.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 34 kinaeleza wakati ambapo nafasi ya Mwenyekiti au mjumbe wa Bodi inakuwa wazi. Hali hii hutokea akijiuzulu kwa notisi ya maandishi kwa mamlaka ya uteuzi, au akikosa mikutano mitatu mfululizo ya Bodi bila ruhusa (ya Mwenyekiti, au ya Waziri kwa upande wa Mwenyekiti). Pia hutokea akishindwa kutekeleza majukumu kwa sababu ya ulemavu au ugonjwa wa mwili au akili, akitangazwa kufilisika na mahakama, au akiingia katika mpango na wadai wake. Vilevile, nafasi inakuwa wazi akikiuka masharti ya Sura ya Sita ya Katiba, au akihukumiwa kifungo cha miezi sita au zaidi kwa kosa.
explanation.sheng: Section 34 ina-say when office ya Chairperson ama member wa Board inakuwa vacant. Hii inafanyika kama ana-resign kwa written notice kwa appointing authority, ama anakosa three meetings za Board in a row without permission (from Chairperson, ama from Cabinet Secretary kama ni Chairperson mwenyewe). Pia inafanyika kama hawezi kufanya kazi because of physical ama mental illness, ana-declared bankrupt na court, ama ana-make arrangement na creditors. Office pia inakuwa vacant kama ana-breach requirements za Chapter Six ya Constitution, ama ana-convicted na ku-sentenced prison for six months ama more.

neutral_check.note: Section only lists the grounds for a Board office becoming vacant; described in plain words without opinion, advice or any view on validity.

clauses.heading: Conduct of business and affairs of the Board.
clauses.text: 35. The provisions of the Schedule shall apply with respect to conduct of the business and affairs of the Board.

explanation.en: This section says that the rules in the Schedule to the Bill apply to how the Board runs its business and affairs. It does not set out those rules itself. They are found in the Schedule.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinasema kwamba masharti yaliyomo katika Jedwali la Mswada huu yanatumika katika uendeshaji wa shughuli na masuala ya Bodi. Kifungu chenyewe hakielezi masharti hayo. Yanapatikana katika Jedwali.
explanation.sheng: Section 35 ina-say kwamba rules za Schedule zina-apply kwa jinsi Board ina-run business na affairs zake. Hii section haiweki hizo rules yenyewe, ziko kwenye Schedule.

neutral_check.note: Procedural section that only points to the Schedule for how the Board conducts its business; explained without opinion.

clauses.heading: Committees of the Board.
clauses.text: 36. The Board may establish such committees as may be appropriate to perform such functions and discharge such responsibilities as it may determine.

explanation.en: This section lets the Board set up committees whenever it thinks they are appropriate. The Board itself decides what work and responsibilities each committee will have.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaruhusu Bodi kuunda kamati inapoona inafaa. Bodi yenyewe ndiyo huamua kazi na majukumu ambayo kila kamati itakuwa nayo.
explanation.sheng: Section 36 ina-allow Board ku-set up committees kama inaona ni appropriate. Board ndiyo ina-decide duties za kila committee.

neutral_check.note: The section only describes an internal power of the Board, so the explanation stays descriptive.

clauses.heading: Delegation.
clauses.text: 37. The Board may delegate to any committee of the Board or to any member staff or agent of the Authority, the exercise of any of the powers or the performance of any of the functions or duties of the Authority under this Act or any other written law.

explanation.en: Section 37 lets the Board hand over some of the Authority's powers, functions or duties to one of the Board's committees, or to a member, staff member or agent of the Authority. This covers powers and duties under this Act and under any other written law (a law that is set out in writing, such as other Acts).
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 37 kinaruhusu Bodi kukabidhi baadhi ya mamlaka, kazi au majukumu ya Mamlaka kwa kamati yoyote ya Bodi, au kwa mjumbe, mfanyakazi au wakala wa Mamlaka. Hii inahusu mamlaka na majukumu chini ya Sheria hii na chini ya sheria nyingine yoyote iliyoandikwa.
explanation.sheng: Section 37 ina-allow Board ku-delegate (ku-hand over) powers, functions ama duties za Authority kwa committee yoyote ya Board, ama kwa member, staff ama agent wa Authority. Hii ina-cover powers na duties under hii Act na under any other written law, yaani other Acts na laws zingine.

neutral_check.note: Section only describes who the Board can hand its powers to; no opinion, advice or legal verdict added.

clauses.heading: Chief Executive Officer.
clauses.text: 38. (1) There shall be a Chief Executive Officer appointed by the Board through an open, transparent, and competitive process. (2) The Chief Executive Officer shall hold office for a term of four years on such terms and conditions of employment as the Board may determine and shall be eligible for re-appointment for one further term of four years subject to satisfactory performance.

explanation.en: This section says the Authority must have a Chief Executive Officer (CEO), chosen by the Board through an open, transparent and competitive process. The CEO serves a four-year term, and the Board decides the terms and conditions of the job. The CEO can be appointed again for one more four-year term, if their performance is satisfactory.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinasema kutakuwa na Afisa Mkuu Mtendaji (CEO), atakayeteuliwa na Bodi kupitia mchakato wa wazi, wa uwazi na wa ushindani. Afisa Mkuu Mtendaji atahudumu kwa muhula wa miaka minne, kwa masharti ya ajira yatakayoamuliwa na Bodi. Anaweza kuteuliwa tena kwa muhula mmoja zaidi wa miaka minne, ikiwa utendaji wake ni wa kuridhisha.
explanation.sheng: Section 38 ina-provide kwamba kuwe na Chief Executive Officer (CEO), ambaye Board ina-appoint through open, transparent na competitive process. CEO ana-serve term ya four years, na Board ndio ina-set terms na conditions za job yake. Anaweza kupewa one more term ya four years, kama performance yake ni satisfactory.

neutral_check.note: Section only describes how the CEO is appointed, the term length and one allowed re-appointment; no opinion added.

clauses.heading: Qualification for appointment as Chief Executive Officer.
clauses.text: 39. A person qualifies to be appointed as a Chief Executive Officer of the Authority if the person— (a) holds a bachelor's degree from a university recognized in Kenya; (b) holds a master’s degree in finance, business administration, education, social science, or other relevant master’s degree from a university recognized in Kenya; (c) has at least fifteen years' experience in the management in a public or private institution, five of which should be in a senior position; and (d) meets the requirements of Chapter Six of the Constitution.

explanation.en: Section 39 sets out who can be appointed as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Authority. A person needs a bachelor's degree and a master's degree (in finance, business administration, education, social science or another relevant field), both from universities recognized in Kenya. The person also needs at least fifteen years' management experience in a public or private institution, with at least five of those years in a senior position, and has to meet the requirements of Chapter Six of the Constitution (on leadership and integrity).
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 39 kinaeleza ni nani anaweza kuteuliwa kuwa Afisa Mkuu Mtendaji wa Mamlaka. Mtu anahitaji shahada ya kwanza na shahada ya uzamili (katika fedha, usimamizi wa biashara, elimu, sayansi ya jamii au fani nyingine husika), zote kutoka vyuo vikuu vinavyotambuliwa nchini Kenya. Pia anahitaji uzoefu wa angalau miaka kumi na mitano katika usimamizi katika taasisi ya umma au ya kibinafsi, ambapo angalau miaka mitano ni katika nafasi ya juu, na kutimiza masharti ya Sura ya Sita ya Katiba (kuhusu uongozi na uadilifu).
explanation.sheng: Section 39 ina-list qualifications za Chief Executive Officer (CEO) wa Authority. Person ana-need bachelor's degree na master's degree (in finance, business administration, education, social science ama other relevant field), both from university recognized in Kenya. Pia ana-need at least fifteen years experience in management kwa public ama private institution, na at least five years kwa senior position, plus ku-meet requirements za Chapter Six ya Constitution (on leadership and integrity).

neutral_check.note: The section only lists appointment qualifications for the CEO; the explanation describes them without opinion, advice or any judgment on legality.

clauses.heading: Functions of the Chief Executive Officer.
clauses.text: 40. The Chief Executive Officer shall— (a) be responsible to the Board of the Authority for the day-to-day management of the affairs of the Authority; (b) be the administrator of the Fund.

explanation.en: This section sets out two duties of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Authority. The CEO is answerable to the Board of the Authority for running its affairs day to day. The CEO is also the administrator of the Fund, which means the person who manages it.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaeleza majukumu mawili ya Afisa Mkuu Mtendaji (CEO) wa Mamlaka. Yeye anawajibika kwa Bodi ya Mamlaka kwa usimamizi wa shughuli za kila siku za Mamlaka. Pia yeye ndiye msimamizi wa Mfuko.
explanation.sheng: Section 40 ina-list duties mbili za Chief Executive Officer (CEO) wa Authority. CEO ni responsible kwa Board ya Authority kwa day-to-day management ya affairs za Authority. Pia ni administrator wa Fund, yaani ndiye ana-manage Fund.

neutral_check.note: Section only describes the CEO's duties and who administers the Fund; explained without opinion, advice or legal judgement.

clauses.heading: Vacancy of the office of the Chief Executive Officer.
clauses.text: 41. (1) The office of the Chief Executive Officer may become vacant if the holder of the office resigns or is removed from office in accordance with subsection (2). (2) The Chief Executive Officer may be removed from office if the Chief Executive Officer is— (e) in breach of chapter six of the Constitution; (f) adjudged bankrupt or enters into a composition scheme or arrangement with his or her creditors; (g) incapacitated by physical or mental illness; or (h) is convicted of a criminal offence and sentenced to imprisonment for a term exceeding six months;

explanation.en: This section says when the office of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) can become vacant: if the CEO resigns or is removed from office. The CEO may be removed for any of these reasons: breaching chapter six of the Constitution (on leadership and integrity), being declared bankrupt or making an arrangement with creditors, being unable to work because of physical or mental illness, or being convicted of a crime and sentenced to prison for more than six months.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaeleza wakati ofisi ya Afisa Mkuu Mtendaji inaweza kuwa wazi: akijiuzulu au akiondolewa ofisini. Afisa Mkuu Mtendaji anaweza kuondolewa akikiuka Sura ya Sita ya Katiba (kuhusu uongozi na maadili), akitangazwa kuwa muflisi au akiingia katika mpango na wadai wake, akishindwa kufanya kazi kwa sababu ya ugonjwa wa mwili au akili, au akihukumiwa kwa kosa la jinai na kufungwa gerezani kwa zaidi ya miezi sita.
explanation.sheng: Section 41 ina-explain wakati office ya CEO inaweza kuwa vacant: CEO ana-resign ama anakuwa removed from office. CEO anaweza kuwa removed kama ana-breach chapter six ya Constitution (leadership na integrity), ametangazwa bankrupt ama ameingia arrangement na creditors, hawezi kufanya kazi because ya physical ama mental illness, ama amekuwa convicted ya crime na sentence ya prison ya more than six months.

neutral_check.note: Describes only when the CEO office becomes vacant and the listed grounds for removal, with no opinion or advice.

clauses.heading: Staff of the Authority.
clauses.text: 42. The Board may appoint such staff as may be necessary for the proper discharge of the functions of the Authority.

explanation.en: This section lets the Board of the Authority appoint (hire) the staff it needs so that the Authority can do its work. It does not say how many staff or what kinds of posts, so the Board decides what is necessary.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaruhusu Bodi kuajiri wafanyakazi wa Mamlaka kadiri wanavyohitajika ili Mamlaka itekeleze majukumu yake ipasavyo. Kifungu hiki hakitaji idadi wala aina ya wafanyakazi, kwa hivyo Bodi ndiyo huamua kinachohitajika.
explanation.sheng: Section 42 ina-allow Board ku-appoint staff wa Authority kama ni needed ili Authority i-do work yake vizuri. Hii section haiweki number ya staff, Board ndio ina-decide ni ngapi.

neutral_check.note: Section only describes the Board's power to appoint staff; no opinion or advice added.

clauses.heading: Establishment of Fund.
clauses.text: 43. There is established a fund to be known as the Tertiary Education Fund which shall be managed and administered by the Authority.

explanation.en: Section 43 sets up a fund called the Tertiary Education Fund. The Authority is the body that manages and administers it. This section only creates the fund and does not itself say where its money comes from or what it is used for.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 43 kinaanzisha hazina inayoitwa Hazina ya Elimu ya Juu (Tertiary Education Fund). Hazina hii itasimamiwa na kuendeshwa na Mamlaka (Authority). Kifungu hiki kinaanzisha hazina tu, hakisemi chenyewe pesa zinatoka wapi wala zinatumika kwa nini.
explanation.sheng: Section 43 ina-establish new fund inaitwa Tertiary Education Fund. Authority ndiyo ina-manage na ku-administer hio fund. Hii section ina-create fund tu, haisemi money inatoka wapi ama inatumika kwa nini.

neutral_check.note: Section only creates a fund and names who manages it; described without opinion. No group tagged because the text itself changes nothing specific for any group.

clauses.heading: Purpose of the Fund.
clauses.text: 44. The purpose of the Fund shall be to provide funds to be granted as education loans under this Act.

explanation.en: This section says what the Fund is for. The Fund exists to provide money that is given out as education loans under this Act.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 44 kinaeleza madhumuni ya Mfuko (Fund). Mfuko huo upo ili kutoa fedha zitakazotolewa kama mikopo ya elimu chini ya Sheria hii.
explanation.sheng: Section 44 ina-state purpose ya Fund. Fund ni ya ku-provide money ya ku-give out kama education loans under hii Act.

neutral_check.note: Section only states the Fund's purpose; the explanation restates it without opinion, advice or any view on legality.

clauses.heading: Sources of funds.
clauses.text: 45. There shall be paid into the Fund— (a) moneys appropriated by the National Assembly; (b) proceeds from investments undertaken by the Authority; (c) repayments of funds disbursed in accordance with this Act or Higher Education Loans Board Act (repealed); (d) interest accrued from the repayments; (e) gifts, grants, donations and endowments; and (f) revenue from any other lawful source.

explanation.en: Section 45 lists where the money paid into the Fund comes from. There are six sources: money the National Assembly appropriates (sets aside by law); proceeds from investments the Authority makes; repayments of funds disbursed under this Act or the repealed Higher Education Loans Board Act; interest accrued from those repayments; gifts, grants, donations and endowments; and revenue from any other lawful source.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 45 kinaorodhesha vyanzo vya pesa zinazolipwa kwenye Mfuko (Fund). Vyanzo ni sita: pesa zilizoidhinishwa na Bunge la Kitaifa; mapato kutokana na uwekezaji unaofanywa na Mamlaka; marejesho ya fedha zilizotolewa chini ya Sheria hii au Sheria ya Bodi ya Mikopo ya Elimu ya Juu (iliyofutwa); riba iliyotokana na marejesho hayo; zawadi, ruzuku, michango na hazina za msaada (endowments); na mapato kutoka chanzo kingine chochote halali.
explanation.sheng: Section 45 ina-list where money ya Fund inatoka. Kuna six sources: money ambayo National Assembly ina-set aside kwa Fund, proceeds from investments za Authority, na repayments ya funds ambazo zili-disbursed under this Act ama repealed Higher Education Loans Board Act. Zingine ni interest from hizo repayments, gifts, grants, donations na endowments, pamoja na revenue from any other lawful source.

neutral_check.note: Section only lists funding sources; described plainly without opinion or advice.

clauses.heading: Eligibility for loans.
clauses.text: 46. (1) Every student or trainee admitted into public or private tertiary institution shall be eligible for an education loan. (2) A student or trainee qualifies to apply for an education loan, if the student or trainee— (a) is a citizen of Kenya; (b) has been admitted in a tertiary institution; and (c) meets the requirements of this Act.

explanation.en: Section 46 says every student or trainee admitted to a public or private tertiary institution (college or university level) is eligible for an education loan. To apply, the person must be a Kenyan citizen, must have been admitted to a tertiary institution, and must meet the other requirements of this Act.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 46 kinasema kila mwanafunzi au mkufunzi aliyekubaliwa kujiunga na taasisi ya elimu ya juu, ya umma au ya kibinafsi, anastahili kuomba mkopo wa elimu. Ili kuomba, mwanafunzi au mkufunzi anapaswa kuwa raia wa Kenya, awe amekubaliwa katika taasisi ya elimu ya juu, na atimize masharti ya Sheria hii.
explanation.sheng: Section 46 ina-say every student ama trainee ambaye ame-get admission kwa public ama private tertiary institution iko na eligibility ya ku-apply education loan. Kuna 3 conditions za ku-qualify: awe citizen wa Kenya, awe ame-get admission kwa tertiary institution, na ame-meet requirements za hii Act.

neutral_check.note: Describes who is eligible to apply for an education loan, without opinion, advice or any view on legality.

clauses.heading: Loans to minors.
clauses.text: 47. An eligible person may apply to the Authority for grant of education loan to a minor who has been admitted to a tertiary institution.

explanation.en: Section 47 lets an eligible person apply to the Authority for an education loan for a minor (a person below the legal age of adulthood) who has been admitted to a tertiary institution. The loan is for the minor, and the application is made by the eligible person. This section does not itself say who counts as an eligible person.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 47 kinamruhusu mtu anayestahiki kuomba mkopo wa elimu kutoka kwa Mamlaka (Authority) kwa ajili ya mtoto mdogo ambaye amekubaliwa katika taasisi ya elimu ya juu. Mkopo ni wa mtoto huyo mdogo, lakini ombi linawasilishwa na mtu anayestahiki. Kifungu hiki hakisemi chenyewe ni nani anayehesabiwa kuwa mtu anayestahiki.
explanation.sheng: Section 47 ina-allow eligible person ku-apply kwa Authority kwa education loan ya minor (child below adult age) ambaye amepata admission kwa tertiary institution. Loan ni ya huyo minor, ila application inafanywa na eligible person. Hii section haisemi eligible person ni nani.

neutral_check.note: The section only describes who may apply for a loan and for whom; the explanation states this without opinion or advice.

clauses.heading: Application for loans.
clauses.text: 48. (1) On admission to a tertiary institution, a student or trainee wishing to be funded shall apply to the Authority in a prescribed manner for the grant of an education loan. (2) The Authority shall review the application and communicate its decision to the applicant and the tertiary institution of the applicant within a prescribed period.

explanation.en: Section 48 explains how a student or trainee asks for an education loan. Under subsection (1), once admitted to a tertiary institution (a college or university), a student or trainee who wants funding applies to the Authority in the way the rules set out. Under subsection (2), the Authority reviews the application and tells both the applicant and their tertiary institution its decision within a period the rules set out.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 48 kinaeleza jinsi mwanafunzi au mwanagenzi anavyoomba mkopo wa elimu. Kifungu kidogo cha (1) kinasema kwamba baada ya kupokelewa katika taasisi ya elimu ya juu, mwanafunzi au mwanagenzi anayetaka kufadhiliwa anawasilisha ombi kwa Mamlaka kwa njia iliyoainishwa. Kifungu kidogo cha (2) kinasema Mamlaka inakagua ombi hilo na kumjulisha mwombaji na taasisi yake uamuzi ndani ya muda ulioainishwa.
explanation.sheng: Section 48 ina-explain jinsi student ama trainee anapata ku-apply kwa education loan. Kwa subsection (1), baada ya admission kwa tertiary institution, student ama trainee ambaye anataka funding ana-apply kwa Authority kwa way ambayo rules zita-set. Kwa subsection (2), Authority ina-review application na ina-tell applicant na tertiary institution yake decision within period ambayo rules zita-set.

neutral_check.note: Describes the application and decision steps only, with no opinion, advice or judgement on legality.

clauses.heading: obligations of the loanee.
clauses.text: 49. (1) A loanee shall, within one year of completion of studies, commence repaying the loan together with any accrued interest and any other charges. (2) A loanee in formal employment shall disclose his or her loan status to the employer at the commencement of employment. (3) A loanee in informal employment shall enter into a payment plan with the Authority on the mode and frequency of payment. (4) In making deductions for loan repayment, the Authority shall deduct not more than twenty five percent of the loanee’s emoluments.

explanation.en: Section 49 sets out what a person with a student loan (a loanee) has to do. Repayment of the loan, with any interest and other charges that have built up, starts within one year after the person finishes studies. A loanee in formal employment tells the employer about the loan when the job starts, and a loanee in informal employment agrees a payment plan with the Authority on how and how often to pay. When the Authority deducts repayments from pay, it can take no more than 25% of the loanee's pay.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 49 kinaeleza majukumu ya mtu mwenye mkopo wa masomo (mkopaji). Mkopaji anaanza kulipa mkopo pamoja na riba iliyokusanyika na gharama nyingine ndani ya mwaka mmoja baada ya kumaliza masomo. Mkopaji aliye katika ajira rasmi anamweleza mwajiri hali ya mkopo wake anapoanza kazi, na aliye katika ajira isiyo rasmi anakubaliana na Mamlaka kuhusu mpango wa malipo, yaani njia na mara ngapi analipa. Mamlaka inapokata malipo kutoka kwa mapato ya mkopaji, haiwezi kukata zaidi ya 25% ya mapato hayo.
explanation.sheng: Section 49 ina-set obligations za loanee (person ambaye ame-take student loan). Loanee anaanza ku-repay loan na interest na charges zingine within one year baada ya ku-finish studies. Loanee kwa formal employment ana-tell employer about loan status yake when job inaanza, na loanee kwa informal employment ana-agree payment plan na Authority on mode na frequency ya payment. Authority ikifanya deductions kutoka pay ya loanee, haiwezi ku-deduct zaidi ya 25%.

neutral_check.note: Describes the loanee's repayment duties, the disclosure and payment plan rules, and the 25% deduction cap without opinion, advice or any judgement on legality.

clauses.heading: Obligations of an employer.
clauses.text: 50. (1) Every employer of a loanee shall— (a) upon employment of a loanee, inform the Authority in writing or in such other manner as the Authority may specify; (b) deduct from the emoluments of the loanee such monthly deductions as may be determined by the Authority until payment in full or exit from their employment whichever is earlier; and (c) remit such deductions within nine days after the end of each month. (2) The Authority shall charge an employer who, after making a deduction from the employee emolument, fails to remit the deductions to the Authority within the prescribed period, a sum equal to five percent of the total amount of the repayment for each month or part of the month that the repayment remains unpaid.

explanation.en: This section sets out what an employer must do when an employee has a student loan from the Authority (a loanee). The employer tells the Authority in writing, or in another way the Authority specifies, when the loanee is employed. The employer deducts the monthly amounts set by the Authority from the loanee's pay until the loan is paid in full or the loanee leaves that job, whichever comes first, and sends them to the Authority within nine days after the end of each month. If an employer makes a deduction but does not send it in time, the Authority charges 5% of the total repayment amount for each month or part of a month it stays unpaid.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaeleza wajibu wa mwajiri wa mkopaji (mtu aliyepewa mkopo na Mamlaka). Mwajiri anaiarifu Mamlaka kwa maandishi, au kwa njia nyingine ambayo Mamlaka itabainisha, mkopaji anapoajiriwa. Mwajiri anakata kiasi cha kila mwezi kilichoamuliwa na Mamlaka kutoka kwa mshahara wa mkopaji hadi deni lilipwe lote au mkopaji aondoke kazini, kutegemea lipi litatangulia, kisha anakipeleka kwa Mamlaka ndani ya siku tisa baada ya mwezi kuisha. Mwajiri akikata lakini asipeleke kwa wakati, Mamlaka inamtoza 5% ya jumla ya malipo ya marejesho kwa kila mwezi au sehemu ya mwezi ambao malipo hayo bado hayajalipwa.
explanation.sheng: Section 50 ina-set obligations za employer wa loanee (person ambaye amechukua loan from the Authority). Employer ana-inform Authority in writing, ama kwa other way ambayo Authority ina-specify, loanee akianza job. Employer ana-deduct monthly amount ambayo Authority ina-decide kutoka pay ya loanee hadi loan iwe paid in full ama loanee a-leave hio job, whichever comes first, na ana-remit hizo deductions within nine days after end ya kila month. Employer akiwa ame-deduct lakini asi-remit on time, Authority ina-charge 5% ya total repayment kwa kila month ama part ya month ambayo repayment iko unpaid.

neutral_check.note: Describes the employer's duties and the 5% charge as the text states them, with no opinion, advice or judgment on legality.

clauses.heading: Debt recovery.
clauses.text: 51. All sums due to the Authority shall be recoverable as debts due to the Authority, and without prejudice to any other remedy, may be recovered by the Authority summarily as a civil debt.

explanation.en: This section says that any money owed to the Authority counts as a debt that the Authority can collect. The Authority can recover it as an ordinary civil debt through a quick court process (called summary recovery). This is in addition to any other way the law already lets the Authority collect the money.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinasema kuwa pesa zote zinazodaiwa na Mamlaka (Authority) ni madeni ambayo Mamlaka inaweza kudai. Mamlaka inaweza kurejesha pesa hizo kama deni la madai (civil debt) kwa njia ya haraka mahakamani. Njia hii haizuii njia nyingine ambazo sheria inaruhusu kurejesha pesa hizo.
explanation.sheng: Section 51 ina-say kwamba all money due kwa Authority ni debt ambayo Authority inaweza ku-recover. Authority inaweza ku-recover hio debt kama civil debt kupitia court process ya haraka, na hio haizuii other ways za ku-recover money.

neutral_check.note: Described only what the section does (debts due to the Authority are recoverable as civil debts), with no opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Data processing.
clauses.text: 52. (1) The Placement Service and the Authority shall maintain a central data repository for purposes of the Act. (2) The Placement Service and the Authority shall manage data through the collection, collation, analysis, reporting, storage, sharing, retrieval, and archiving of information related to— (a) related placement and funding of students or trainees; (b) students and trainees enrolled in tertiary institutions outside Kenya; (c) career guidance; and (d) other matters. (3) The repository shall contain information on— (a) students funded by the Authority; (b) repayment of loans; and (c) placement of students.

explanation.en: This section requires the Placement Service and the Authority to keep one central data repository for the purposes of the Act. They are to collect, analyse, report on, store, share, retrieve and archive information on placement and funding of students or trainees, students and trainees enrolled in tertiary institutions outside Kenya, career guidance, and other matters. The repository must hold information on students funded by the Authority, repayment of loans, and placement of students.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaagiza Placement Service na Authority kuweka hifadhi kuu moja ya data kwa madhumuni ya Sheria hii. Zinatakiwa kukusanya, kuchambua, kuripoti, kuhifadhi, kushiriki, kupata na kuweka kwenye kumbukumbu taarifa kuhusu upangaji na ufadhili wa wanafunzi au wanagenzi, wanafunzi walioandikishwa katika taasisi za elimu ya juu nje ya Kenya, ushauri wa kikazi, na mambo mengine. Hifadhi hiyo lazima iwe na taarifa kuhusu wanafunzi wanaofadhiliwa na Authority, ulipaji wa mikopo, na upangaji wa wanafunzi.
explanation.sheng: Section 52 ina-require Placement Service na Authority ku-maintain central data repository kwa purposes za Act. Wana-manage data kwa ku-collect, analyse, report, store, share, retrieve na archive information on placement na funding ya students ama trainees, students ambao wame-enroll kwa tertiary institutions outside Kenya, career guidance na other matters. Hii repository ina-contain information on students ambao Authority ina-fund, loan repayment na placement ya students.

neutral_check.note: Describes the duty to keep a central data repository and what it must hold, without opinion, advice or any view on legality.

clauses.heading: Data sharing. Cap. 411C.
clauses.text: 53. Notwithstanding any other written law, the Authority may request a person or entity to furnish it with any data in line with the Data Protection Act to enable it perform its functions under thisAct. (2) The Authority shall utilize the existing relevant government and third-party databases in the performance of its functions.

explanation.en: Section 53 lets the Authority ask any person or organisation to give it data it needs to do its work under this Act, even if another written law says something different. The request has to be in line with the Data Protection Act. Subsection (2) says the Authority is to use the government and third-party databases that already exist when it does its work.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 53 kinaruhusu Mamlaka kumwomba mtu yeyote au shirika limpe data inayohitajika kutekeleza majukumu yake chini ya Sheria hii, hata kama sheria nyingine iliyoandikwa inasema tofauti. Ombi hilo linapaswa kuwa kwa mujibu wa Sheria ya Ulinzi wa Data (Data Protection Act). Kifungu kidogo cha (2) kinaitaka Mamlaka itumie hifadhidata za serikali na za wahusika wengine ambazo tayari zipo.
explanation.sheng: Section 53 ina-allow Authority ku-request data kutoka kwa any person ama organisation, hata kama kuna other written law inasema tofauti. Hio request ni lazima iwe in line na Data Protection Act, na data ni ya ku-help Authority ifanye kazi yake under hii Act. Subsection (2) ina-require Authority itumie existing databases za government na third parties.

neutral_check.note: Section only describes the Authority's power to request data and its duty to use existing databases; no opinion or verdict added.

clauses.heading: Alternative dispute resolution.
clauses.text: 54. Any dispute arising under this Act shall be referred to the Placement Service or the Authority, as the case may be, for resolution through alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.

explanation.en: This section says that any dispute that comes up under this Act is sent to the Placement Service or the Authority, depending on which one the matter concerns. That body then handles it through alternative dispute resolution, which means ways of settling a disagreement other than a court case.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinasema kwamba mgogoro wowote unaotokea chini ya Sheria hii unapelekwa kwa Placement Service au Mamlaka (Authority), kulingana na suala husika. Mgogoro huo unatatuliwa kupitia njia mbadala za kutatua migogoro.
explanation.sheng: Section 54 ina-say kwamba any dispute under hii Act ina-go kwa Placement Service ama Authority, depending on which one ina-handle hio matter. Hio dispute ina-resolvewa kupitia alternative dispute resolution, ambayo ni other ways za ku-settle dispute.

neutral_check.note: Describes only who handles disputes and how, with no opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Financial year.
clauses.text: 55. The financial year of the Placement Service and Authority shall be the period of twelve months ending on the thirtieth of June in each year.

explanation.en: This section sets the financial year of the Placement Service and the Authority. It is the twelve months ending on 30 June each year.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaweka mwaka wa fedha wa Huduma ya Upangaji (Placement Service) na Mamlaka (Authority). Ni kipindi cha miezi kumi na miwili kinachoisha tarehe 30 Juni kila mwaka.
explanation.sheng: Section 55 ina-set financial year ya Placement Service na Authority. Financial year ni period ya twelve months ambayo ina-end 30 June every year.

neutral_check.note: Technical clause fixing a financial year date for two public bodies; described plainly with no opinion.

clauses.heading: Annual estimates.
clauses.text: 56. (1) The Placement Service and the Authority shall, within three months after the end of each financial year, cause to be prepared estimates of its revenue and expenditure for that financial year. (2) The annual estimates shall make provision for estimated expenditure of the Placement Service and the Authority for the financial year concerned, and in particular shall provide for– (a) the grant of the loans and scholarships for students in tertiary institutions; (b) the funding for the infrastructure in public tertiary institutions; (c) the payment of salaries, allowances, pensions, gratuities, and other charges in respect of the staff and members of the Placement Service and the Authority; and (d) the proper maintenance of any property vested in the Placement Service and the Authority. (3) The annual estimates shall be approved by the respective Boards before the commencement of the financial year to which they relate and after the approval, the annual estimates shall not be increased without the prior consent of the Board. (4) No expenditure shall be incurred for the purposes of the Placement Service or the Authority except in accordance with the annual estimates approved under subsection

explanation.en: This section requires the Placement Service and the Authority to prepare yearly estimates of their income and spending within three months after the end of each financial year. The estimates must provide for loans and scholarships for tertiary students, funding for infrastructure in public tertiary institutions, pay and other staff costs, and upkeep of property. Each Board must approve its estimates before the financial year starts, and after that they cannot be increased without the Board's prior consent. Spending must follow the approved estimates.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaitaka Huduma ya Upangaji (Placement Service) na Mamlaka (Authority) kuandaa makadirio ya kila mwaka ya mapato na matumizi ndani ya miezi mitatu baada ya mwisho wa kila mwaka wa fedha. Makadirio hayo lazima yatoe nafasi ya mikopo na ufadhili wa masomo kwa wanafunzi wa taasisi za elimu ya juu, fedha za miundombinu katika taasisi za umma za elimu ya juu, mishahara na malipo mengine ya wafanyakazi, na utunzaji wa mali. Kila Bodi lazima iidhinishe makadirio yake kabla ya mwaka wa fedha kuanza, na baada ya hapo hayawezi kuongezwa bila idhini ya awali ya Bodi. Matumizi lazima yafuate makadirio yaliyoidhinishwa.
explanation.sheng: Section 56 ina-require Placement Service na Authority ku-prepare annual estimates za revenue na expenditure within three months after the end ya each financial year. Hizo estimates must include loans na scholarships kwa students wa tertiary institutions, funding ya infrastructure kwa public tertiary institutions, salaries na other staff costs, na maintenance ya property. Each Board ina-approve estimates before financial year i-start, na after approval estimates can't be increased without prior consent ya Board. All expenditure must follow approved estimates.

neutral_check.note: Describes the estimates process and required budget items only, with no opinion or advice. The clause text ends mid-sentence at subsection (4), so only what is written is explained.

clauses.heading: Books of accounts and audit.
clauses.text: 57. (1) The Placement Service and the Authority shall cause to be kept all proper books and records of accounts of the income, expenditure, assets and liabilities of the Placement Service and the Authority. (2) Within a period of three months after the end of each financial year, the Placement Service and the Authority shall submit to the Auditor-General the accounts of that year together with a statement of– (a) the income and expenditure of the Placement Service and the Authority during that year; and (b) the assets and liabilities of the Placement Service and the Authority as at the last day of the financial year. (3) The annual accounts of the Placement Service and the Authority shall be prepared, audited, and reported in accordance with the Constitution and the Public Audit Act.

explanation.en: Section 57 requires the Placement Service and the Authority to keep proper books and records of their income, spending, assets and debts. Within three months after each financial year ends, each of them must send that year's accounts to the Auditor-General. These must include a statement of income and expenditure for the year and a statement of assets and liabilities as at the last day of the year. The accounts are prepared, audited and reported under the Constitution and the Public Audit Act.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 57 kinaitaka Huduma ya Upangaji (Placement Service) na Mamlaka (Authority) kutunza vitabu na rekodi sahihi za mapato, matumizi, mali na madeni yao. Ndani ya miezi mitatu baada ya mwaka wa fedha kuisha, kila moja inapaswa kuwasilisha hesabu za mwaka huo kwa Mkaguzi Mkuu wa Hesabu za Serikali (Auditor-General). Hesabu hizo ziambatane na taarifa ya mapato na matumizi ya mwaka, na taarifa ya mali na madeni hadi siku ya mwisho ya mwaka. Hesabu hizo huandaliwa, hukaguliwa na kuripotiwa kwa mujibu wa Katiba na Sheria ya Ukaguzi wa Umma (Public Audit Act).
explanation.sheng: Section 57 ina-require Placement Service na Authority ku-keep proper books and records za income, expenditure, assets na liabilities zao. Within three months after financial year ina-end, kila moja ina-submit accounts za hio year kwa Auditor-General, pamoja na statement ya income and expenditure na statement ya assets and liabilities as at last day ya year. Hizo accounts ni za ku-prepare, ku-audit na ku-report kulingana na Constitution na Public Audit Act.

neutral_check.note: Section only sets record-keeping and audit duties for two public bodies; described in plain terms with no judgement on policy or legality.

clauses.heading: Protection from personal liability.
clauses.text: 58. No matter or thing done by the Chairperson or a member of the Board or any officer, employee or agent of the Placement Service and the Authority shall, if the matter or thing is done bona fide for the purpose of executing any provision of this Act, render the Chairperson, member, officer, employee or agent or any person acting on their directions, personally liable to any action, claim or demand whatsoever.

explanation.en: This section says that the Chairperson, a Board member, or an officer, employee or agent of the Placement Service and the Authority cannot be held personally responsible in any action, claim or demand for something they did in good faith to carry out this Act. The same protection covers anyone acting on their directions.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinasema kwamba Mwenyekiti, mjumbe wa Bodi, au afisa, mwajiriwa ama wakala wa Huduma ya Upangaji (Placement Service) na Mamlaka hawawezi kuwajibishwa binafsi katika shauri, madai au matakwa yoyote kwa jambo walilofanya kwa nia njema ili kutekeleza masharti ya Sheria hii. Ulinzi huu pia unawahusu watu wanaofanya kazi kwa maagizo yao.
explanation.sheng: Section 58 ina-say Chairperson, member wa Board, na officer, employee ama agent wa Placement Service na Authority hawawezi ku-be sued personally kwa action, claim ama demand yoyote, kama walifanya hio thing kwa good faith ili ku-execute hii Act. Hio protection pia iko kwa any person anafanya kazi kwa directions zao.

neutral_check.note: Described only who is covered and what the protection does, with no opinion on it and no comment on its legal effect.

clauses.heading: Common seal.
clauses.text: 59. (1) The common seal of the Placement Service and the Authority shall be kept in the custody of the Chief Executive Officer and shall not be used except on the direction of the Board. (2) The affixing of the common seal of the Placement Service or the Authority shall be authenticated by the signatures of the Chairperson and the Chief Executive Officer.

explanation.en: This section covers the common seal (the official stamp) of the Placement Service and of the Authority. The Chief Executive Officer keeps the seal, and it can only be used when the Board directs. Whenever the seal is put on a document, the Chairperson and the Chief Executive Officer both sign to confirm it.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinahusu muhuri wa pamoja (common seal) wa Huduma ya Upangaji (Placement Service) na wa Mamlaka (Authority). Muhuri hutunzwa na Afisa Mkuu Mtendaji, na hautumiwi bila maelekezo ya Bodi. Muhuri unapowekwa kwenye hati, saini za Mwenyekiti na Afisa Mkuu Mtendaji zinathibitisha matumizi hayo.
explanation.sheng: Section 59 ina-cover common seal (official stamp) ya Placement Service na ya Authority. Chief Executive Officer ndiye ana-keep seal, na seal haiwezi ku-be used bila direction ya Board. Seal ikiwekwa kwa document, Chairperson na Chief Executive Officer wana-sign ku-confirm.

neutral_check.note: Describes who keeps the seal and how its use is authorised and confirmed; no opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Amendment of Cap 22.
clauses.text: 60. Section 42 of the Limitation of Actions Act is amended in subsection (1) by deleting paragraph (i) and substituting therefor the following new paragraph– (i) civil proceedings brought under the Tertiary Education Placement and Funding Act for the recovery of any loans owed to the Authority including any penalty or interest thereon.

explanation.en: This section changes section 42(1) of the Limitation of Actions Act, the law that sets time limits for taking cases to court. It deletes paragraph (i) and puts in a new paragraph about civil court cases under the Tertiary Education Placement and Funding Act to recover loans owed to the Authority, including any penalty or interest on them. Section 42 is the list of matters that the Limitation of Actions Act does not apply to.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinabadilisha kifungu cha 42(1) cha Limitation of Actions Act, sheria inayoweka muda wa kupeleka kesi mahakamani. Kinafuta aya (i) na kuweka aya mpya kuhusu kesi za madai chini ya Tertiary Education Placement and Funding Act za kurejesha mikopo inayodaiwa na Mamlaka (Authority), pamoja na faini au riba yoyote. Kifungu cha 42 ni orodha ya mambo ambayo Limitation of Actions Act haitumiki kwayo.
explanation.sheng: Section 60 ina-change Section 42(1) ya Limitation of Actions Act, sheria ambayo ina-set time limits za kupeleka cases court. Ina-repeal na ku-replace paragraph (i) na new paragraph ya civil cases chini ya Tertiary Education Placement and Funding Act za ku-recover loans za Authority, pamoja na penalty na interest. Section 42 ni list ya cases ambazo Limitation of Actions Act haina-apply.

neutral_check.note: Technical amendment to a list in the Limitation of Actions Act; described only what it changes, with no opinion or advice.

clauses.heading: Liability for damages.
clauses.text: 61. The provisions of this Act shall not relieve the Placement Service and the Authority of the liability to pay compensation or damages to any person for any injury to the person, their property or any of their interest caused by the exercise of any power conferred by this Act or by the failure, whether wholly or partially of the exercise of such powers.

explanation.en: Section 61 says this Act does not remove the duty of the Placement Service and the Authority to pay compensation or damages to any person. This covers injury to a person, their property or their interests. It applies whether the harm came from using a power given by the Act, or from failing, wholly or partly, to use that power.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 61 kinasema kwamba Sheria hii haiondoi wajibu wa Placement Service na Authority wa kulipa fidia au gharama za madhara kwa mtu yeyote. Hii inahusu madhara kwa mtu, mali yake au maslahi yake. Inatumika iwe madhara yametokana na kutumia mamlaka yaliyotolewa na Sheria hii, au na kushindwa kuyatumia, kwa ukamilifu au kwa sehemu.
explanation.sheng: Section 61 ina-say kwamba hii Act haita-remove liability ya Placement Service na Authority ya ku-pay compensation ama damages kwa any person. Hii ni kwa injury kwa person, property yake ama interests zake, kama injury ime-happen kwa sababu ya ku-use powers za hii Act, ama kwa sababu ya ku-fail ku-use hizo powers, wholly ama partially.

neutral_check.note: Describes only who stays liable for compensation and for what harm; no opinion, advice or verdict on legality.

clauses.heading: General penalty.
clauses.text: 62. A person convicted of an offence under this Act for which no other penalty is prescribed shall be liable to a fine not exceeding one million shillings or, in the case of a natural person, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or to both.

explanation.en: This section sets the penalty for any offence under this Act that has no penalty of its own. A person convicted can be fined up to one million shillings. If the person is a natural person (an individual, not a company), the court can instead impose up to two years in prison, or both the fine and the prison term.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaweka adhabu kwa kosa lolote chini ya Sheria hii ambalo halina adhabu nyingine iliyotajwa. Mtu aliyepatikana na hatia anaweza kutozwa faini isiyozidi shilingi milioni moja. Kama ni mtu binafsi (si kampuni), anaweza kufungwa gerezani kwa muda usiozidi miaka miwili, au kupewa adhabu zote mbili.
explanation.sheng: Section 62 ina-set general penalty kwa offence yoyote chini ya hii Act ambayo haiko na penalty yake yenyewe. Person akiwa convicted anaweza kulipa fine ya hadi one million shillings. Kama ni individual (sio company), court inaweza pia kum-jail kwa hadi two years, ama fine na jail zote mbili.

neutral_check.note: Describes the penalty range only, with no opinion on its fairness or effect.

clauses.heading: Regulations.
clauses.text: 63. (1) The Cabinet Secretary may make regulations for the better carrying out the provisions of this Act. (2) Without prejudice to subregulation (1), the regulations under subregulation (1) may provide for the following— (a) placement of students and trainees; (b) the receipt, processing, and approval of applications for education loans and the forms required; (c) review on placement and funding; (d) loans to minors; (e) the withdrawal, suspension, the recovery, exemption, cancellation, and waiver of loans; (f) recovery of loans from loanees residing outside Kenya; (g) funding of students and trainees outside Kenya. (h) career guidance; and (i) such other necessary for giving full effect to the implementation of this Act

explanation.en: Section 63 allows the Cabinet Secretary to make regulations to help carry out this Act. The regulations may cover: placement of students and trainees; receiving, processing and approving education loan applications and the forms to be used; review of placement and funding; loans to minors; withdrawing, suspending, recovering, exempting, cancelling and waiving loans; recovering loans from borrowers living outside Kenya; funding students and trainees studying outside Kenya; career guidance; and any other matter needed to give full effect to the Act.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 63 kinampa Waziri mamlaka ya kutunga kanuni za kusaidia kutekeleza Sheria hii. Kanuni hizo zinaweza kuhusu: kupangiwa nafasi kwa wanafunzi na wanagenzi; kupokea, kushughulikia na kuidhinisha maombi ya mikopo ya elimu pamoja na fomu zitakazotumika; mapitio ya upangaji nafasi na ufadhili; mikopo kwa watoto walio chini ya umri wa utu uzima; kusitisha, kusimamisha, kurejesha, kusamehe, kufuta na kuondoa madeni ya mikopo; kurejesha mikopo kutoka kwa wakopaji wanaoishi nje ya Kenya; ufadhili wa wanafunzi na wanagenzi walio nje ya Kenya; ushauri wa kitaaluma wa taaluma; na jambo lingine lolote linalohitajika ili Sheria hii itekelezwe kikamilifu.
explanation.sheng: Section 63 ina-let Cabinet Secretary ku-make regulations za ku-help hii Act ifanye kazi. Hizo regulations zinaweza ku-cover: placement ya students na trainees; ku-receive, ku-process na ku-approve applications za education loans na forms za kutumia; review ya placement na funding; loans kwa minors; ku-withdraw, ku-suspend, ku-recover, ku-exempt, ku-cancel na ku-waive loans; ku-recover loans kutoka kwa loanees ambao wanaishi outside Kenya; funding ya students na trainees outside Kenya; career guidance; na other matters ambazo zinahitajika ku-give full effect kwa hii Act.

neutral_check.note: Describes the regulation-making power and lists each item it may cover, with no opinion or advice.

clauses.heading: Repeal. Cap. 213. Cap. 210. Cap. 210A.
clauses.text: 64. (1) The Higher Education Loans Board Act is repealed. (2) Part VII and VIII of the Universities Act are repealed. (3) Part IX of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act is repealed.

explanation.en: Section 64 repeals three pieces of existing law. It removes the whole Higher Education Loans Board Act, Parts VII and VIII of the Universities Act, and Part IX of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act. To repeal means to take them out of the law, so they stop being law.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 64 kinafuta sehemu tatu za sheria zilizopo. Kinafuta Sheria nzima ya Higher Education Loans Board (Bodi ya Mikopo ya Elimu ya Juu), Sehemu VII na VIII za Sheria ya Vyuo Vikuu, na Sehemu IX ya Sheria ya Elimu na Mafunzo ya Ufundi na Stadi (TVET). Kufuta kunamaanisha kuziondoa katika sheria, kwa hivyo hazitakuwa sheria tena.
explanation.sheng: Section 64 ina-repeal three laws: whole Higher Education Loans Board Act, Part VII na Part VIII ya Universities Act, na Part IX ya Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act. Ku-repeal ni ku-remove hizo laws na parts, so zina-stop kuwa law.

neutral_check.note: Describes only which laws and Parts are repealed, with no opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Transition. Cap. 210.
clauses.text: 65. (1) The Kenya University and Colleges Central Placement Service shall be the successor to the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service Board established under section 55 (repealed) of the Universities Act. (2) The Tertiary Education Funding Authority shall be the successor to— (a) the Higher Education Loans Management Board established under section 3 of the Higher Education Loans Board Act (repealed). (b) the Universities Fund Board established under section 53 (repealed) of the Universities Act; and (c) the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Funding Board established under section 47 (repealed) of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act.

explanation.en: This section says which new bodies take over from old ones. The Kenya University and Colleges Central Placement Service succeeds the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service Board, which was set up under section 55 of the Universities Act (repealed). The Tertiary Education Funding Authority succeeds three bodies: the Higher Education Loans Management Board (Higher Education Loans Board Act, repealed), the Universities Fund Board (section 53 of the Universities Act, repealed) and the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Funding Board (section 47 of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act, repealed).
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinataja vyombo vipya vinavyochukua nafasi ya vyombo vya zamani. Kenya University and Colleges Central Placement Service ni mrithi wa Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service Board, kilichoanzishwa chini ya kifungu cha 55 cha Sheria ya Vyuo Vikuu (iliyofutwa). Tertiary Education Funding Authority ni mrithi wa vyombo vitatu: Higher Education Loans Management Board (Sheria ya Higher Education Loans Board, iliyofutwa), Universities Fund Board (kifungu cha 53 cha Sheria ya Vyuo Vikuu, kilichofutwa) na Technical and Vocational Education and Training Funding Board (kifungu cha 47 cha Sheria ya Technical and Vocational Education and Training, kilichofutwa).
explanation.sheng: Section 65 ina-name successors wa old bodies. Kenya University and Colleges Central Placement Service ina-take over kutoka Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service Board (section 55 ya Universities Act, repealed). Tertiary Education Funding Authority ina-take over kutoka three bodies: Higher Education Loans Management Board (Higher Education Loans Board Act, repealed), Universities Fund Board (section 53 ya Universities Act, repealed) na Technical and Vocational Education and Training Funding Board (section 47 ya Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act, repealed).

neutral_check.note: Transition clause that only names which government bodies succeed which; described without opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Transfer of property, assets and liabilities.
clauses.text: 66. (1) All references to the former institutions in any agreement or instrument relating to any property, assets, rights, obligations or liabilities transferred under subsections (2) and (3) and subsisting immediately before the commencement of this Act, shall at the commencement of this Act, unless the context otherwise requires be read as references to the Placement Service and the Authority respectively. (2) All movable and immovable property and assets which immediately before the commencement of this Act were vested in or possessed by the former institutions, shall, at the commencement of this Act, vest in the Service and the Authority respectively without further conveyance, transfer or assignment. (3) All rights, obligations, assets, liabilities which immediately before the commencement of this Act were vested in or imposed on the former institutions, shall, at the commencement of this Act, be deemed to be the rights, obligations, assets and liabilities of the Service and the Authority respectively. (4) All actions, suits or legal proceedings pending by or against the former institutions shall, at the commencement of this Act, be deemed to be actions, suits, or legal proceedings against the Service or the Authority.

explanation.en: This section moves the property, assets, rights, obligations and debts (liabilities) of the former institutions to the Placement Service and the Authority, each taking over its own share, on the day the Act starts. Property and assets pass over automatically, with no separate transfer papers needed. Any agreement that names a former institution is read as naming the Placement Service or the Authority instead, unless the context requires otherwise. Court cases already under way for or against a former institution are treated as cases for or against the Service or the Authority.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 66 kinahamisha mali, haki, wajibu na madeni ya taasisi za awali kwa Huduma ya Uwekaji (Placement Service) na Mamlaka (Authority), kila moja kwa upande wake, Sheria hii inapoanza kutumika. Mali inahamishwa moja kwa moja bila hati za ziada za uhamisho. Mikataba inayotaja taasisi za awali itasomwa kana kwamba inataja Huduma ya Uwekaji au Mamlaka, na kesi zinazoendelea mahakamani zitahesabiwa kuwa kesi dhidi ya Huduma au Mamlaka.
explanation.sheng: Section 66 ina-transfer property, assets, rights, obligations na liabilities za former institutions kwa Placement Service na Authority, each one kwa part yake, from the day Act ina-start. Property na assets ina-move automatically, na hakuna further paperwork ya transfer. Agreements zote ambazo zina-mention former institutions zita-be read kama zina-mention Placement Service na Authority, na court cases pending against former institutions zita-be against Service ama Authority.

neutral_check.note: Section only moves property, rights, liabilities and pending cases between public bodies, described without opinion.

clauses.heading: Staff.
clauses.text: 67. Any person who, immediately before the commencement date of this Act, was a member of staff of the former institutions shall be deemed to be members of staff of the Service and Authority respectively.

explanation.en: This section deals with staff of the former institutions. Anyone who was a member of staff of a former institution just before this Act starts is treated as a member of staff of the Service or the Authority, as the case may be. It is a transition rule: the staff become staff of the new bodies, and the section does not describe their pay or terms.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 67 kinahusu wafanyakazi wa taasisi za awali. Mtu yeyote aliyekuwa mfanyakazi wa taasisi ya awali mara moja kabla ya tarehe ya kuanza kutumika kwa Sheria hii atachukuliwa kuwa mfanyakazi wa Huduma (Service) au wa Mamlaka (Authority), kwa mtiririko huo. Hii ni kanuni ya mpito, na kifungu hiki hakieleezi mshahara wala masharti ya kazi.
explanation.sheng: Section 67 ina-cover staff ya former institutions. Any person ambaye alikuwa staff ya former institution just before date ambayo hii Act ina-start atakuwa counted kama staff ya Service ama Authority, kila moja kwa yake (respectively). Ni transition rule tu, na hii section haisemi chochote kuhusu pay ama terms za staff.

neutral_check.note: Described only the transfer of staff status to the Service and Authority, with no opinion, advice or legal judgement.

clauses.heading: Interpretation of this Part. Cap. 213. Cap. 210. Cap. 210A.
clauses.text: 68. In this Part— “former institutions” means the Higher Education Loans Management Board established under the Higher Education Loans Boards Act, the Universities Fund Board, the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service established under the Universities Act, and the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Funding Board established under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act.

explanation.en: Section 68 explains what the words "former institutions" mean in this Part of the Bill. They mean four bodies: the Higher Education Loans Management Board (set up under the Higher Education Loans Boards Act), the Universities Fund Board, the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (set up under the Universities Act), and the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Funding Board (set up under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act). It is a definitions clause only and does not change anything else.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 68 kinafafanua maana ya maneno "former institutions" (taasisi za zamani) katika Sehemu hii ya Mswada. Maneno hayo yanamaanisha taasisi nne: Bodi ya Usimamizi wa Mikopo ya Elimu ya Juu (iliyoanzishwa chini ya Sheria ya Bodi za Mikopo ya Elimu ya Juu), Bodi ya Hazina ya Vyuo Vikuu, Huduma ya Kati ya Upangaji wa Wanafunzi katika Vyuo Vikuu na Vyuo (iliyoanzishwa chini ya Sheria ya Vyuo Vikuu), na Bodi ya Ufadhili wa Mafunzo ya Ufundi na Kiufundi (iliyoanzishwa chini ya Sheria ya Mafunzo ya Ufundi na Kiufundi). Kifungu hiki ni cha tafsiri tu na hakibadilishi kitu kingine.
explanation.sheng: Section 68 ina-define term "former institutions" kwa hii Part ya Bill. Ina-mean four bodies: Higher Education Loans Management Board (chini ya Higher Education Loans Boards Act), Universities Fund Board, Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (chini ya Universities Act), na Technical and Vocational Education and Training Funding Board (chini ya Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act). Hii section ni definition only, haifanyi change nyingine.

neutral_check.note: Definitions clause only; explanation lists the four named bodies with no opinion, advice or legal judgement.

text.en: On 6 October 2026 the Education Committee told the National Assembly it was analysing the views it had received, and planned to go through the Bill clause by clause with major stakeholders from 12 to 16 October. After that, it tables its report in the House for the Second Reading of the Bill.
text.sw: Tarehe 6 Oktoba 2026 Education Committee iliambia Bunge la Kitaifa kwamba ilikuwa ikichambua maoni iliyopokea, na ilipanga kupitia Mswada kifungu kwa kifungu pamoja na wadau wakuu kuanzia 12 hadi 16 Oktoba. Baada ya hapo, inawasilisha ripoti yake Bungeni kwa ajili ya Kusomwa kwa Mara ya Pili kwa Mswada huo.
text.sheng: On 6 October 2026 Education Committee ili-tell National Assembly kwamba ilikuwa ina-analyse views ambazo ili-receive, na ilikuwa ina-plan ku-go through hii Bill clause by clause na major stakeholders from 12 to 16 October. After hapo, ina-table report yake kwa House for the Second Reading ya hii Bill.

requirements.en: Written memoranda, as invited by the Clerk of the National Assembly's public notice of 18 August 2026. The Committee also held public hearings in all 47 counties, from 14 September to 2 October 2026. Email and postal details for this Bill were not found in an official notice online.
requirements.sw: Memoranda zilizoandikwa, kama zilivyoalikwa na tangazo la umma la Clerk of the National Assembly la tarehe 18 Agosti 2026. Kamati pia ilifanya vikao vya hadhara katika kaunti zote 47, kuanzia 14 Septemba hadi 2 Oktoba 2026. Maelezo ya barua pepe na posta kwa Mswada huu hayakupatikana katika tangazo rasmi mtandaoni.
requirements.sheng: Written memoranda, kwa public notice ya Clerk of the National Assembly ya 18 August 2026, ambayo ina-invite hizo memoranda. Committee pia ili-hold public hearings kwa all 47 counties, from 14 September to 2 October 2026. Email na postal details za hii Bill hazikuwa found kwa official notice online.
